headline: Asian stocks bounced on Friday after Thursday's AI-driven tech rout, helped by Nvidia chief Jensen Huang defending CoreWeave's finances.
score_reason: Next-day rebound report from AFP via Yahoo; useful context for the sell-off; facts support the pool score.
importance_line: Fund holders saw a one-day recovery after a sharp fall, but Huang is a supplier defending a customer, and the rebound does not remove the inflation and rate worries behind the sell-off.
summary: AFP reports that Seoul rose more than 2% and Tokyo about 1.8% on Friday 16 Oct 2026 after slumping 7.6% and 4.9% on Thursday, as traders awaited remarks from US Federal Reserve head Kevin Warsh at the IMF meetings in Bangkok. After CoreWeave, a data centre operator that borrowed heavily to buy Nvidia chips, fell 15.5% on Wednesday, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang told Bloomberg that its cost of capital is falling, which SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes said helped lift AI shares.
notes: Pool source Yahoo Finance; the Yahoo page metadata names AFP as provider, so AFP is credited. Item is dated Friday 16 Oct 2026 and describes Thursday's rout.
